Re-ran the full corpus walk from HEAD with the same methodology: 44 comparison.head edits across 32 single-parent commits (not 50/38), 38 with endingCommit present (not 44), 36 agreeing (not 42), split 33 creations and 3 modifications (not 34/8). The 2 disagreements are unchanged, same commit f7fc4ef88, same two logs, so the ADR's central negative example survives. This does not reopen the Decision (unchanged reasoning: it rests on binding.commit being a rarely-read fallback, the security lens's adversarial-bypass measurement, and the check never reaching a committed log, none of which this corpus measures), but it downgrades the hand-sync claim throughout from a measured, seven-instance corpus finding to an independently documented but never-committed example (the PR #4954 finding against session-14695/session-15001, closed with a reply because that session had exhausted its commit budget).
